summary: 1. High-stayed hooks start immediately with interactive mental imagery ('Socho...') or shocking counter-intuitive statements instead of background context. 2. Combining pop-science topics (dinosaurs, physics) with everyday familiar objects (cars, teeth) drastically improves retention and initial views. 3. Short, bold Hindi titles with prominent emojis perform significantly better than passive English or technical descriptive titles. 4. Videos with delayed hooks or generic informational setups fail the 3-second test and suffer drop-offs below 35% stayed_pct. 5. High average view duration requires concrete visual metaphors (e.g., '3 cars on your teeth') right in the first sentence to lock viewer attention.
winning_hooks: Interactive mental visualization: Starting with 'Socho...' (Imagine...) and giving an extreme visual metaphor (e.g., '3 small cars stacked on your teeth').
Counter-intuitive bold claims: Stating a paradox upfront (e.g., 'A car that crumples in a crash is the one that saves your life').
avoid: Dry, descriptive English/Hinglish intro sentences that summarize the topic instead of creating a narrative gap.
Technical educational titles without high-stakes curiosity or emojis (e.g., 'Common Household Items That Contain Radioactive Materials').
Slow setup questions that explain context before reaching the core punchline.
next_experiment: Test an A/B variation using the 'Socho...' (Imagine...) visual hook formula on a physics/tech topic versus a direct question hook, keeping video length under 45 seconds.
